title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical company handbook entry for new and existing Redwood employees covering: what it’s like to work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, the hiring and onboarding lifecycle, and the internal tools we use day-to-day. It is maintained by People Ops with contributions from Engineering Managers and the Growth org.

Key points:
- Clear expectations for each role and promotion criteria.
- Standardized hiring and interview steps to reduce bias.
- A practical onboarding checklist (first 30/90 days).
- Essential internal tools, access steps, and owners.

1. Working at Redwood — culture and values

We prioritize a production-first engineering culture, psychological safety, and continuous learning. Our core values are:
- Build for reliability and customers.
- Ship fast, measure, iterate.
- Be deliberate and kind.
- Share knowledge broadly.

Working model
- Core hours: flexible; teams coordinate for overlap windows.
- Remote-first with optional office hubs in major regions.
- Travel: occasional offsites and customer visits; travel policies are in People Ops.

2. Roles & career ladders (engineering & cross-functional summary)

Purpose: provide transparent expectations for progression and hiring bands. Managers should share role profiles during hiring and performance conversations.

Engineering ladder (summary):
- IC1 / New Grad: learns codebase, delivers small features with oversight.
- IC2 / Software Engineer: independently owns tasks, writes tests, participates in designs.
- IC3 / Senior Software Engineer: designs subsystems, mentors others, drives delivery for medium-sized projects.
- IC4 / Staff Engineer: leads cross-team design, influences architecture, sets standards.
- IC5 / Principal / Distinguished: company-level technical leadership, long-term strategy.

Product & Design ladder (summary):
- Associate PM/Designer -> PM/Designer -> Senior -> Lead/Staff -> Director+

Managerial path
- Engineering Manager (EM) levels correlate with span and scope: EM1 (team), EM2 (multiple teams), EM3 (platform/organization). Promotion criteria focus on people leadership, delivery outcomes, and organizational impact.

Promotion expectations (what you need to demonstrate):
- Consistent delivery of scoped outcomes.
- Clear evidence of impact (metrics, product/customer feedback).
- Growing scope: mentoring, cross-team influence, or product leadership.
- Alignment with company values and collaboration norms.

Role profile table (example for IC3 / Senior Software Engineer):
| Area | Expectation | Example evidence |
|------|-------------|------------------|
| Delivery | Owns features end-to-end | Completed a major feature with monitoring and rollback plan |
| Design | Proposes scalable designs | PR with architecture notes and perf considerations |
| Quality | Writes tests and handles incidents | Reduced incident frequency; authored runbooks |
| Mentorship | Coaches junior engineers | Regular 1:1s, onboarding buddies, tech talks |

3. Benefits & perks (summary)

Redwood provides a competitive benefits package designed for early/mid-stage startup growth employees. Key highlights:

- Compensation: market-competitive base + equity grants structured by role and level.
- Health: medical, dental, and vision plans (US/EU region variants).
- Retirement: 401(k) plan with company match (US) / equivalent pension guidance for other regions.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO baseline (pro-rated), parental leave policy, paid holidays.
- Professional development: annual learning stipend, conference budget, internal training days.
- Wellness: mental health coverage, EAP, stipend for home-office equipment.
- Remote work support: home-office stipend, co-working allowance where available.

Perks & extras
- Free or discounted access to partner tools (design tools, learning platforms).
- Regular knowledge-sharing events, tech talks, and an annual offsite.
- Referral bonuses and internal recognition programs.

How to find detailed plan documents
- Benefits vendor pages (linked in the People Ops portal).
- Submit benefits questions to benefits@redwood.ai.

4. Hiring process overview (roles & interview standards)

Goals: hire fairly, hire for potential, and maintain a consistent candidate experience. Hiring steps (standardized):
1) Requisition approval and role profile created by hiring manager.
2) Sourcing & outreach (recruiter lead).
3) Phone screen (30–45 min) — cultural fit + role basics.
4) Technical/functional interviews (2–4 rounds) — role-specific rubric applied.
5) Hiring manager loop and leadership calibration.
6) Offer & negotiation; candidate references; background check (where required).

Interview rubrics and bias reduction
- Use standardized rubrics stored in the Recruiting folder. Each interviewer must submit scorecards and written feedback.
- At least one interviewer trained in inclusive interviewing on each loop.

Typical timelines
- From first screen to offer: target 2–4 weeks for senior roles, 1–3 weeks for IC1–IC2.

Hiring committee & approvals
- Hiring manager + recruiter propose level and budget. For senior hires, a hiring packet is reviewed by the hiring committee (includes manager, teammate, People Ops reviewer).

5. Onboarding: first 30 / 60 / 90 day checklist

Objective: make new hires productive and integrated into the team and Redwood culture quickly. Onboarding is jointly owned by People Ops, the hiring manager, and the buddy.

Pre-Start (People Ops):
- Complete offer paperwork, set up payroll details, enroll in benefits.
- Invite to Slack, Okta, and company calendar.
- Provision GitHub and cloud access (request: infra-access@g.redwood.ai).

Day 0–7 (Welcome & orientation):
- Orientation session: company mission, org overview, security basics.
- Team intro and first 1:1 scheduled with manager.
- Complete mandatory trainings (security, privacy, code of conduct).
- Set up dev environment following the repo quickstart (link in team README).

Days 8–30 (Deliver early wins):
- Join team ceremonies (standup, planning).
- Complete 2 small onboarding tasks (example PRs) to validate environment.
- Meet cross-functional partners: product, design, SRE.
- First feedback checkpoint at 30 days between manager and new hire.

Days 31–90 (Broader impact & learning):
- Lead a small project or own a feature milestone.
- Begin career development planning with manager.
- 90-day review: discuss progress, open goals, and health of onboarding.

Onboarding checklist (condensed):
- [ ] Access: Slack, Okta, Google Workspace, GitHub, CI, cloud console
- [ ] Paperwork: NDAs, tax, benefits enrollment
- [ ] Training: Security, data handling, compliance courses
- [ ] Tech setup: local dev, tests pass, CI pipelines triggered
- [ ] Social: intro meetings, buddy check-ins, team lunch/virtual coffee

6. Internal tools guide (practical quickstart & owners)

This section lists the core tools, purpose, how to get access, and primary owner. If you need access that is not automated, open a ticket with IT via the People Ops portal.

Core tools (quick reference)
- Slack — company communication
  - Purpose: async & real-time communication, channels by team and topic.
  - Access: invited pre-start; join #announcements, #engineering, and your team channel.
  - Owner: People Ops / IT.

- Okta (SSO) — single sign-on and MFA
  - Purpose: centralized authentication to all SSO-enabled apps.
  - Access: People Ops issues invitation; enroll MFA (recommended: mobile authenticator + security key).
  - Owner: Security & IT.

- GitHub (source control)
  - Purpose: code hosting, PR reviews, CI triggers.
  - Access: invite to org; request team membership via team-admins.
  - Owner: Eng Dev Tools.
  - Quick tips: follow the PR template, add changelog notes, and include test coverage.

- CI/CD (Buildkite / GitHub Actions)
  - Purpose: build/test/deploy automation.
  - Access: GitHub permission + pipeline role.
  - Owner: Platform SRE.

- Cloud console (GCP / AWS)
  - Purpose: environment visibility and troubleshooting.
  - Access: role-based grant; require approval from infrastructure oncall for elevated permissions.
  - Owner: Cloud Infrastructure.

- Confluence (internal docs)
  - Purpose: canonical documentation and handbooks.
  - Access: default read for employees; write access by request for non-owners.
  - Owner: People Ops / Documentation Guild.

- Notion / Marketing Hub (product docs & go-to-market content)
  - Purpose: cross-functional product and GTM docs.
  - Access: request via People Ops.

- Support & Escalation (Zendesk / Internal triage)
  - Purpose: customer tickets and internal escalation playbooks.
  - Access: product or CS roles; emergency oncall via PagerDuty.

- Expense & Finance tools (Ramp / Expensify)
  - Purpose: submit expenses and corporate card management.
  - Access: finance-ops request; training required for high limits.

How to request access (steps)
1) Confirm the tool in the onboarding checklist.
2) Submit access request via People Ops portal with manager approval.
3) Security performs role review; expect < 48 hours for standard tools.

Security & compliance notes
- MFA is mandatory for all accounts with access to production systems.
- Never share credentials; use company-approved password managers.
- Follow the data classification and handling doc for customer data.

7. Manager & Buddy responsibilities

Manager responsibilities (first 90 days):
- Schedule recurring 1:1s and set clear first-90 day goals.
- Ensure onboarding tasks are assigned and tracked.
- Provide timely feedback and remove blockers.

Buddy role (peer mentor):
- Provide day-to-day help for the first 30 days.
- Review team practices, review PRs, and make introductions.

8. Career development & performance reviews

- Performance cycles: biannual formal reviews with mid-cycle check-ins.
- Career conversations: documented development plans, promotion timelines, and mentorship matching.
- Calibration: managers participate in level calibration sessions to ensure consistency across teams.

Promotion packet checklist
- Updated résumé-style summary of achievements (1–2 pages).
- Examples of work (PRs, design documents, metrics).
- Peer/manager feedback and a proposed new role profile.

9. Returning or relocating employees

- If you go on leave or return from long-term absence, People Ops will coordinate re-onboarding and benefits updates.
- For international relocations, review tax and benefits implications with Finance and People Ops at least 60 days ahead.

10. Where to find help

- People Ops portal (primary): benefits, payroll, time off, and access requests.
- IT & Security tickets: security@redwood.ai or via the People Ops portal.
- Manager: first point of contact for role questions and performance feedback.

Appendix: Templates & links
- 30/90 day goal template (link in People Ops templates).
- Interview scorecard template (Recruiting folder).
- PR/Code review checklist (Engineering docs).

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (Jordan Patel).
- Review cadence: annual or as policy changes.
- Change process: submit suggested edits through the Confluence suggestions flow; major policy changes require People Ops + Legal review.

This handbook page is intended to be a concise, actionable reference. For more detailed policy artifacts (tax, region-specific benefits, parental leave specifics), consult the People Ops benefits binder or contact People Ops directly.
